chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one who reverts (to his wife) and did not keep witnesses, he said: 'Witnessing is more beloved to me, and I do not see any problem with what he has done'.

key_terms.يُرَاجِعُ: He reverts (to his wife after a revocable divorce)
key_terms.يُشْهِدْ: He keeps witnesses / He makes them witness

ai.seo_question: Is it mandatory to have witnesses when a man reverts to his wife after a revocable divorce?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the status of witnesses in marital reversion (*ruju'*), distinguishing between the recommended practice (*mustahabb*) and the essential validity (*sahih*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that while public declaration via witnesses is preferred to prevent disputes, the act remains legally binding even if performed privately, emphasizing the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding marital procedures.
